question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Minimum for compensation and a baseline autofluorescence gate you need one negative/autofluorescence control and one single colour compensation control per detector.

With 5 detectors

* 1 x unstained / beads only / autofluorescence control for voltage and negative population placement
* 1 x AF350 single stain compensation control
* 1 x GFP single stain compensation control
* 1 x PE single stain compensation control
* 1 x AF647 single stain compensation control
* 1 x AF750 single stain compensation control

= 5 +1 = 6 tubes.  On streptavidin capture beads the 5 single stain controls can be made as 5 separate bead aliquots saturated with biotinylated AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 streptavidin conjugates and an unstained bead aliquot for the negative baseline. The 5 single stains are the set that is used for spectral compensation, the unstained set is used for autofluorescence, voltage and initial gate placement.

That is the compensation minimum. For a sort the gating position is as important as the compensation. Best practice for a 5 colour sort is to add a Fluorescence Minus One control for each parameter to define the positive gate in the presence of spillover from the other 4 fluorochromes. That is 5 FMO tubes in addition to the 6 compensation/baseline tubes, i.e. 11 tubes in total for a rigorous sort set-up, 6 of which are strictly required for compensation and baseline.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a sorting experiment the non-negotiable part of the set-up is a negative/un-stained reference and a compensation reference for every fluorochrome that will be used in the sort.

With a 5 colour panel

* AF350
* GFP
* PE
* AF647
* AF750

the compensation set can be generated on streptavidin-capture beads. 
One bead tube stained with each individual biotinylated-fluorochrome conjugate is required for spectral unmixing/compensation, i.e. 5 single-stain bead controls. 
One unstained bead / unstained cell negative control is required to set background, autofluorescence and the sort threshold.

That is the n + 1 minimum that is required to run the cytometer and to sort:

5 single-colour streptavidin-bead compensation controls + 1 unstained/negative control = 6 essential controls

The same 5 single-stain beads are normally also used as the positive spill-over references for the instrument. If a cell negative control is kept separate from the bead negative control you will have 7 tubes in practice: 5 bead singles + 1 bead alone + 1 unstained cells.

For rigorous sort gate placement the panel is normally run with Fluorescence Minus One controls, 1 FMO per channel, and many labs also add an isotype/ biological negative. In that best practice set-up you have:

1 unstained/negative
5 single-stain compensation
5 FMO

= 11 tubes in addition to the experimental samples, 6 of which are the absolute minimum required to compensate and to define a negative population for a 5-colour sort.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a sorting experiment you must be able to set a negative gate and you must be able to compensate the panel. That is the non-negotiable minimum.

* 1x negative / unstained control
The beads alone, or cells/beads with no fluorochrome, is required to set the autofluorescence/baseline and the negative gate for sorting. With streptavidin beads this is the streptavidin bead only / unstained bead control.

* 1x single colour compensation control per detection channel
Compensation is set on a singly stained population in the same matrix you will sort. Streptavidin beads are routinely used as a compensation bead matrix because a biotinylated fluorochrome-conjugate will bind the beads.  One compensated single-stain bead tube is needed per fluorochrome that will be used in the sort:

AF350 single-stain bead
GFP single-stain bead
PE single-stain bead
AF647 single-stain bead
AF750 single-stain bead

That is 1 unstained + 5 single-stain = 6 essential tubes for correct signal detection and compensation.

In practice for a 5-colour sort you will want robust gating as well.  Best practice then adds a Fluorescence Minus One control for each channel to define spill-over dependent boundaries, 5 FMO + the unstained already counted, i.e. 1 unstained + 5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 11 tubes for full panel optimisation. The 6 tubes above are the absolute essential minimum for a compensated, sortable data set.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d call for 10 essential controls for this 5-color sort with streptavidin beads. You need one unstained/negative baseline to set autofluorescence and gate boundaries, five single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls — one each for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 — to build an accurate spillover matrix for the sorter, and four FMO controls. With five parameters the FMO for the last channel recapitulates the unstained baseline for sorting purposes, so the informative FMOs are n-1. That is 1 unstained + 5 single-stains + 4 FMOs = 10 controls that are strictly required to set compensation and validate gating before sorting.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a 5-color sort on AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 I would prepare 10 essential controls.

1 unstained / autofluorescence control for the cell line/bead population to set the negative baseline and define FSC/SSC gates.

5 single-stain compensation controls, one per reporter, run on streptavidin beads or capture beads matched to the experiment. That is AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 each alone so the spillover matrix can be built accurately for all five detection channels.

4 fluorescence minus one controls. FMO for AF350, FMO for GFP, FMO for PE and FMO for AF647 are needed to define the positive gate boundaries in the presence of the other four fluorophores and to check for spectral spillover. The FMO for AF750 is essentially the unstained population in practice once the four visible/visible-NIR channels are present, so the unstained control already covers the last channel’s background for sorting purposes.

That gives 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls that are truly required to set compensation, gates and sort purity for the streptavidin bead panel.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a 5-colour sort the compensation matrix and a negative reference have to be defined on the same matrix / bead matrix that will be used in the sample.

* 1 x blank / unstained streptavidin bead control. This is the negative/auto-fluorescence reference for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 and the baseline for the sort gate.
* 1 x single colour compensation control per reporter that will be used in the panel. With streptavidin beads the single colour can be set up as biotinylated antibody – fluorophore saturating a streptavidin bead, i.e.

  * AF350-streptavidin bead
  * GFP-streptavidin bead
  * PE-streptavidin bead
  * AF647-streptavidin bead
  * AF750-streptavidin bead

That is 5 single-stain compensation controls + 1 unstained/blank = 6 essential bead controls for compensation and negative reference.

That is the minimal essential set to generate a usable compensation matrix and to set a negative sort gate. In practice for a sort you want a robust gate definition as well. The routinely added rigorous set is 5 Fluroescence Minus One controls, one per channel, to define spill-over-defined negatives for gating:

5 single-stain compensation beads + 1 unstained bead + 5 FMOs = 11 controls

which collapses to the 6 compensation + negative controls above if FMOs are not formally run. Isotype / biological positive controls for the biology of interest are additional to the instrument controls.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about a 5-channel sort using streptavidin beads: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750.

Core consensus from round 0:
* Non-negotiable instrument controls are a negative/autofluorescence baseline and one single-stain compensation control per detection channel, run in the same matrix as the sort.
* With streptavidin beads the single-stains are made by saturating bead aliquots with biotinylated fluor-conjugates, and the baseline is unstained beads / beads only.
* Minimal counting: 1 unstained/negative + 5 single-stain = 6 tubes. Colleagues 1,2,3,5 all state this as the absolute minimum for a usable compensation matrix and negative sort gate. Colleague 3 notes in practice 7 tubes if a separate unstained cell control is kept besides bead alone.

Disagreement is about FMOs and what counts as “essential” for sorting:
* Colleagues 1,2,3,5: best practice/rigorous sort adds 5 Fluorescence Minus One controls, one per channel, to define positive gates in presence of spillover. That gives 1 unstained +5 single +5 FMO = 11 tubes for full panel optimisation, with 6 being the strict minimum. Isotype/biological positives are additional.
* Colleagues 4,6: argue 10 controls are strictly required for compensation + validated gating. They count 1 unstained +5 single-stains +4 FMOs =10, reasoning the FMO for the last channel, AF750, recapitulates the unstained baseline for sorting purposes, so n-1 informative FMOs are needed. 

Important claims/evidence preserved:
* Compensation matrix must be built on the same bead matrix as samples.
* Unstained control sets autofluorescence, voltage and initial gate placement.
* FMOs are used for spill-over defined negatives and gate placement, not for compensation.
* Unstained control also serves as baseline for voltage and negative population placement.

Unresolved for me:
* Definition of “essential” in the prompt: minimal to run/compensate vs minimal to reliably sort with purity. If strictly instrument minimum, answer is 6. If gate validation is included as essential for sorting, answer is 11 by the majority, or 10 per the n-1 FMO argument.

Current belief leaning: the universally agreed minimum is 6 tubes; FMOs are best practice and often treated as essential for sorting, giving 11 tubes in the most cited rigorous set. The 10-tube n-1 FMO variant is a minority optimization argument.

6.text:

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Thanks for laying out the compensation core so clearly. I think we’re all aligned on the non-negotiable instrument minimum for this streptavidin bead sort: one unstained/beads-only control to set autofluorescence, voltage and the negative sort boundary, plus one single-stain streptavidin bead control per detection channel for the spillover matrix. That is 1 unstained + AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 single-stains = 6 tubes, and that is what you absolutely need to get a compensated, sortable data set.

Where the set expands is gating validation. For a sort you do need to see where the positive population sits in the presence of spillover from the other 4 fluorochromes. FMOs are the way to define that, but they are not all independent for this panel. The four visible/near-visible channels AF350, GFP, PE and AF647 all have measurable spillover into each other and into the far-red detector. An FMO for each of those four defines a spillover-dependent negative that cannot be inferred from the unstained bead alone.

The AF750 FMO is a different case. AF750 is in the far-red/NIR window and its spillover into AF350, GFP, PE and AF647 is essentially negligible; conversely the spillover from the four shorter wavelength dyes into the AF750 channel is the only thing that would shift its background. That background shift is already captured by the unstained bead control, and by the four FMOs that remove AF350/GFP/PE/AF647 one at a time. Once those four are present, the AF750-minus-all-others condition recapitulates the unstained bead baseline for sorting purposes, so it does not add independent gate information for this matrix.

* 1 x unstained streptavidin bead / autofluorescence control
* 5 x single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
* 4 x informative FMOs: FMO AF350, FMO GFP, FMO PE, FMO AF647

1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls that are strictly required to build the compensation matrix and to set spillover-correct positive gates before sorting. The fifth FMO and extra biological/isotype controls are best practice for robustness and publication-grade panel optimisation, but they are not essential to run a compensated sort on this 5-channel bead system.

1 unstained / beads only
5 single-stain compensation beads: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
5 FMO beads: AF350 FMO, GFP FMO, PE FMO, AF647 FMO, AF750 FMO

1.text:
For a streptavidin bead sort the matrix on which you build the compensation and gating controls has to be the same matrix you sort.

Instrument non-negotiable on that matrix is:

* 1 x unstained / beads only autofluorescence baseline to set voltages, FSC/SSC and the negative population placement for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 x single-stain compensation control per detection channel made on streptavidin beads saturated with the biotinylated fluor-conjugate
 AF350 bead, GFP bead, PE bead, AF647 bead, AF750 bead

That is 1 + 5 = 6 tubes, the n+1 minimum to build a usable spillover matrix and to have a negative reference. That is agreed by all colleagues and is the minimum to get compensated data out of the sorter.

A compensation matrix alone does not define where a positive sort gate sits in the presence of spillover from the other four fluorochromes. For a sort gate validation you need spillover-defined negatives.

Unstained = no fluor present.
FMO AF750 = AF350+GFP+PE+AF647 present.

Hence the AF750 detector sees the spillover from AF350, GFP, PE and AF647 into AF750 in the FMO AF750 tube, which is absent in the unstained bead tube. The same spillover-dependence is true for each of the other four channels. The unstained baseline and the AF750 FMO are therefore not equivalent for gate placement in the AF750 channel, and the same logic holds for AF350, GFP, PE and AF647.

A gate-validated sort set on this 5-colour bead panel is therefore:

1 unstained/beads only
5 single-stain bead compensation controls: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
5 FMOs: FMO AF350 = GFP+PE+AF647+AF750; FMO GFP = AF350+PE+AF647+AF750; FMO PE = AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750; FMO AF647 = AF350+GFP+PE+AF750; FMO AF750 = AF350+GFP+PE+AF647

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes for compensation + validated gating.

That is the rigorous set that colleagues 1,2,3,5 describe and which in practice is treated as essential for sort purity. The 6-tube set is the strict instrument minimum, and isotype/biological positive controls are additional to these instrument controls.

The n-1 FMO = 10 control argument collapses the AF750 FMO onto the unstained baseline on the basis that AF750 spills essentially nowhere. Even accepting negligible forward spillover from AF750, the reverse spillover from the four shorter dyes into the AF750 detector is real and is not present in the unstained beads-only tube. That spillover-into-AF750 information is needed for an accurate AF750 sort gate and is why the textbook 5 FMO set is retained for a 5-channel sort.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: Thanks for the clear breakdown of the compensation core. I agree with Colleagues 1,2,3,5 on the instrument non-negotiables for a streptavidin bead sort on this panel.

On the same bead matrix we need:
* 1 x unstained / beads-only autofluorescence reference for voltage, autofluorescence baseline and negative sort placement for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750
* 1 x single-stain compensation control per detector made on streptavidin beads: AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750

That is 1 + 5 = 6 tubes, the absolute minimum to build a spillover matrix and run compensated data. That part is settled.

Where the question of “essential” comes in is gate validation for sorting. A sort gate has to be placed in the presence of spillover from the other four fluorochromes, so FMOs are the way to define a spillover-defined negative. * 5 single-stain compensation beads AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
* 4 informative FMOs: FMO AF350, FMO GFP, FMO PE, FMO AF647

1 + 5 + 4 = 10 controls.

* 1 x single-stain compensation control per detection channel made on saturated streptavidin beads with biotinylated fluor-conjugate: AF350 bead, GFP bead, PE bead, AF647 bead, AF750 bead

That minimum gets you compensated data. It does not get you a validated sort gate.

1 unstained/beads only
5 single-stain bead compensation controls
5 FMOs on beads:

FMO GFP   = AF350+PE+AF647+AF750
FMO PE    = AF350+GFP+AF647+AF750
FMO AF647 = AF350+GFP+PE+AF750
FMO AF750 = AF350+GFP+PE+AF647

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes for compensation + validated gating.

Colleague 4 and Colleague 6 make a reasonable spectral-directionality point: AF750 has essentially no forward spillover into AF350/GFP/PE/AF647, and the reverse spillover from the four shorter dyes into AF750 is small relative to bead autofluorescence. After perfect compensation the FMO and unstained would converge, but empirical gate placement in a sort needs the FMO measurement.

1 unstained beads only
5 single-stain compensation beads AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750
4 informative FMOs: FMO AF350, FMO GFP, FMO PE, FMO AF647
